title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
header:
Date: 2025-10-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Mark Rivera (Acuity CTO), Sara Li (Platform Eng), Ibrahim Khan (Security), Nina Park (SRE)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest performance tests on Redwood Private (VPC) pilot, discuss networking/routing issues observed during canary, review upcoming control-plane upgrade window, and agree next steps for firewall rules and final benchmarks.
topics: networking: VPC peering, firewall ports, NAT gateway
routing: service endpoints, egress rules, proxy configuration
security: KMS, audit logs, SOC 2 items
action_items: Priya Shah - share updated network diagram and required CIDR/ports - due 2025-10-10
Sara Li - confirm firewall rules applied to dev VPC and share NAT gateway IPs - due 2025-10-09
Alex Kim - send trimmed benchmark spreadsheet (p95/p99) + test harness details - due 2025-10-11
Ibrahim Khan - provide list of compliance questions for SOC2 doc pack - due 2025-10-15
Daniel Ortiz - schedule rollback/runbook review with Acuity SREs for upgrade window - due 2025-10-12
next_steps: Redwood to push control-plane upgrade to staging Thursday night (10/09) and report results
Customer to validate connectivity after firewall changes and report any packet loss or route asymmetry
Both teams to align on final benchmark set for go/no-go decision next week
Set up a short joint runbook readthrough before production upgrade
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining today's weekly sync, um let's do a quick roll call, i think we have the usuals.
[00:08] Mark Rivera: yep Mark here.
[00:12] Sara Li: Sara on the line.
[00:15] Ibrahim Khan: Ibrahim.
[00:18] Nina Park: Nina here.
[00:22] Alex Kim: cool, quick agenda - network follow ups, the routing anomalies from last night's canary, the control plane upgrade schedule, and benchmarks. priya i'll hand to you for the test results?
[00:32] Priya Shah: sure yeah uh so we ran the canary across the dev VPC between 00:30 and 02:00 UTC - results attached in the spreadsheet Alex will share, overall token throughput is stable, p50 around 120ms, p95 jumped to 450ms on a handful of requests, that's the spike we think is tied to routing through the NAT gateway and a transient route flap.
[01:05] Sara Li: when you say route flap, is that internal to the Acuity VPC or the peering connection?
[01:10] Priya Shah: good q - logs show path divergence at the peering boundary, so packets from the Redwood control-plane endpoint briefly took a different egress, leading to asymmetric paths and higher latency. sometimes the health checks recovered but there was a 30-45s window with retries.
[01:35] Nina Park: we saw retransmits in our tcp logs too; the SRE team suspected MTU issues at first but packet captures point at routing changes.
[01:45] Ibrahim Khan: is there anything on the Redwood side that can cause that? we did not change routing rules.
[01:50] Priya Shah: we did a small routing optimization yesterday - it shouldn't have touched peering rules, but possible the BGP session refresh caused transient reroutes; i'm tracking that.
[02:05] Alex Kim: okay action: Priya will post the exact timestamps and flows so your team can correlate.
[02:12] Priya Shah: yep will do.
[02:15] Mark Rivera: second topic - the public/private endpoint split, we wanted private endpoints only in our pilot; some of the test traffic hit the public control endpoint by mistake yesterday.
[02:30] Alex Kim: mmh, thanks Mark. i think that was a misconfiguration in the test harness where the environment variable pointed to the hosted endpoint. Daniel, can you confirm?
[02:40] Daniel Ortiz: yeah that was on our side, we had an env var fallback. i've flagged the harness to prefer the VPC private endpoint now. we've also added a guard so it fails loudly if public endpoints are used in the pilot env.
[02:58] Sara Li: great, once that's fixed we'll re-run the full smoke test. any implications for keys or KMS?
[03:05] Priya Shah: our KMS integration is per-tenant; for the private deploy you're using customer-managed keys via the HSM connector - that was in place and worked in the tests. there was one permission error for the audit log bucket which we fixed.
[03:25] Ibrahim Khan: can you send the minimal IAM policy we need? security wants the exact ARNs.
[03:30] Alex Kim: yes, Priya i'll attach the IAM snippet to the ticket.
[03:35] Priya Shah: note though, some of the log delivery goes via our control plane; for the private model we push aggregated audit logs to your bucket with encryption CMKs you control.
[03:48] Nina Park: good. on the upgrade - you mentioned control-plane 1.5, is that the one with the faster KV cache invalidation?
[03:55] Priya Shah: exactly, 1.5 has KV cache bugfixes and better prefix caching which should reduce cold-start tokens and lower p95. we want to roll to staging Thursday night and target production next week if staging looks clean.
[04:10] Mark Rivera: is there a rollback plan? last time an upgrade caused a brief outage for us.
[04:15] Alex Kim: yes we've prepared a rollback runbook, Daniel will coordinate a readthrough with your SREs. it includes steps to fail traffic to hosted fallback and revert control-plane config.
[04:28] Daniel Ortiz: i'll set up a 30-minute runbook run next Tue with your team; tentative Wed upgrade window if everything passes.
[04:38] Sara Li: for the staging run we need the list of tests to run - smoke, latency, and heavy token load. can you share the harness config?
[04:45] Priya Shah: i'll post the harness repo and the exact curl/load scripts. they include tokenized workloads and deterministic prompts so we can compare model outputs. note that the quantization profile differs slightly for private vs hosted so expect minor output divergence.
[05:05] Ibrahim Khan: does that affect quality checks? we have some end-to-end evals.
[05:09] Priya Shah: it can, but our optimize tool flags regression if output embedding distance crosses threshold; we'll run that as part of the benchmark.
[05:20] Alex Kim: moving on - firewall ports. we still need confirmation that 443 outbound to the control-plane IPs is allowed plus ephemeral ranges for data plane. Sara?
[05:30] Sara Li: ok we opened 443 but the ephemeral ports were blocked by policy; we can open them but need an exact port list.
[05:38] Priya Shah: the recommended ephemeral range is 10240-65535 for short-lived data connections; however the control plane uses a pinned set too - i'll include both ranges and specific CIDRs in the diagram.
[05:53] Nina Park: do you have a static list of control-plane IPs? NAT makes them change for us.
[05:58] Priya Shah: for the pilot we'll give you the current CIDR set and a low-churn list; in private mode the control-plane sits in your VPC so it should be stable.
[06:10] Mark Rivera: earlier you mentioned some requests went to hosted fallback - how does fallback work in private?
[06:16] Priya Shah: by policy - we prefer private local model endpoints, then dedicated if available, and finally hosted as a last-resort fallback. in pilot we can disable hosted fallback if you want to ensure no data leaves the VPC.
[06:30] Ibrahim Khan: yes please, until compliance sign-off we want fallback disabled.
[06:34] Alex Kim: noted, we'll flip that flag for the pilot env.
[06:38] Priya Shah: also we found a config mismatch where the KV cache TTL was set very low in your staging harness, causing more cache misses and raising token usage; bumping TTL to 300s helped.
[06:50] Nina Park: ok we'll align that in the harness.
[06:54] Mark Rivera: what's left for go/no-go?
[06:58] Alex Kim: 1) confirm no routing flaps after peering fix, 2) successful staging upgrade with KV improvements, 3) bench thresholds met (p95 < 300ms for our key flows), 4) security sign-off on KMS/IAM.
[07:15] Sara Li: can you quantify the bench thresholds and share the spreadsheet?
[07:18] Alex Kim: yes i'll share a trimmed spreadsheet showing p50/p95/p99 and token/sec per model.
[07:24] Priya Shah: note the p95 target varies by prompt length; we'll include grouped results.
[07:30] Mark Rivera: one more item - audit logs retention and access. we need a retention policy and an RBAC map.
[07:36] Ibrahim Khan: also we need proof of SOC2 controls around log integrity.
[07:40] Alex Kim: Priya will attach the SOC2 controls summary and the retention config we propose.
[07:46] Priya Shah: yes i'll paste that to the ticket.
[07:50] Daniel Ortiz: action recap - i'll schedule runbook readthrough, Priya posts network diagram and harness, Alex sends benchmark spreadsheet, Sara validates firewall and NAT, Ibrahim compiles compliance Qs.
[08:04] Mark Rivera: timeline wise we aim to decide next Wed after staging run, is that okay?
[08:09] Alex Kim: that works. any last questions?
[08:13] Sara Li: none from me.
[08:15] Nina Park: no.
[08:17] Ibrahim Khan: okay thanks all.
[08:20] Alex Kim: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts. meeting adjourned.
[08:25] (call ends)

Notes: transcription includes minor mis-hearings; references to NAT/gateway/peering and KV cache abbreviated in places. Links shared in chat: (1) benchmark spreadsheet - link to google drive, (2) network diagram - link to confluence, (3) SOC2 summary doc - internal redwood link.
